scenes.narration: Apple announced four new products in September, and then put the old prices up.

data.headline: Apple, September 2026
data.subtext: Four products, and a price rise

scenes.narration: Welcome back. Today we're going through Apple's whole September event — the iPhone 18 Pro, the first foldable iPhone, two watches, new AirPods, and the prices. So why did last year's iPhones get dearer the day the new one arrived?

Start with the iPhone 18 Pro. Its body is the same size as last year's, and the camera plateau that runs the full width of the back arrived on the 17 Pro, so it isn't new — it's about two millimetres shallower. What is new sits inside it: three cameras, a flash, the lidar scanner, and underneath, a vapor chamber with three times the surface area to move heat away from the chip.

appleStage.headline: The plateau is [shallower], not new
appleStage.caption: iPhone 18 Pro, from the back
appleStage.premise: Drawn from Apple's own dimensions: 71.9 by 150 millimetres, 8.75 deep.

scenes.narration: Now the real headline, which is the aperture. Apple gave the main camera six laser-cut blades that open to f one point four eight, which is the widest an iPhone has gone, so a dim room stops looking like one. Close them down to f four and the whole scene comes into focus instead. Until now, changing that on a phone meant changing the photo in software.

appleStage.headline: Six blades, [f/1.48] to f/4
appleStage.caption: A real variable aperture
appleStage.premise: The blades move. This is glass and metal, not a background blur applied afterwards.

scenes.narration: Here's how Apple puts it on the iPhone 18 Pro page. The new variable aperture on the main camera adjusts for better lighting and depth of field automatically, so everything from candid portraits to cinematic video looks its best. Automatically is the word doing the work there, because the phone picks the stop for you, which means the feature only shows up as pictures that came out better than you expected.

recordedStep.sourceNote: Apple, iPhone 18 Pro product page, captured 10 September 2026
recordedStep.caption: Apple's own words for it

scenes.narration: Running all of it is the A20 Pro, and it's the first phone chip built on a two nanometre process — smaller transistors, so more of them fit in the same space. Six CPU cores: two big ones Apple calls super cores, twenty percent quicker than last year, and four efficiency cores for everything a phone does while you aren't looking at it.

appleStage.headline: A20 Pro: the first [2nm] phone chip
appleStage.caption: Apple's own floorplan
appleStage.premise: Two super cores, four efficiency cores, a seven-core GPU and a 32-core Neural Engine.

scenes.narration: Then Apple did the thing it had never done before. The iPhone Duo folds: shut, the outer screen is a whole phone, one-handed. Open the hinge and the inner display is close to a small tablet — the largest screen Apple has ever put on an iPhone, and the thinnest one it has made, because half the electronics sit on the other side of the fold.

appleStage.headline: A phone that opens into [a tablet]
appleStage.caption: iPhone Duo, shut and open
appleStage.premise: Both states to the same scale: the cover screen, and the inner display it opens to.

scenes.narration: Here's the detail worth stopping on. On that inner display the FaceTime camera sits underneath the screen, so there's no notch, no punch hole and no island breaking the surface — the camera only surfaces when something asks for it. Every rival foldable still puts a hole in its big screen.

appleStage.headline: The camera is [under] the screen
appleStage.caption: Under-display FaceTime camera
appleStage.premise: The camera lives beneath the panel and only appears when an app calls for it.

scenes.narration: Two halves and a hinge have to weigh something, and the Duo weighs two hundred and fifty four grams against two hundred and eleven for an iPhone 18 Pro. Forty three grams reads as nothing written down and feels like something in a shirt pocket. Pricing starts at one thousand nine hundred and ninety nine dollars, eight hundred more than the Pro.

appleStage.headline: [254 grams], and $1,999
appleStage.caption: Weight, in grams
appleStage.premise: Both figures are Apple's own, for the base configuration of each phone.

scenes.narration: Watches came next, and there are two. Series 12 is the smaller pair, forty six millimetres or forty two, and this year in ceramic as well as aluminium and titanium. Ultra 4 is the big one — forty nine millimetres of grade five titanium, with an Action Button on the left edge, because a gloved hand finds an edge faster than a screen.

appleStage.headline: Series 12, and the [Ultra 4]
appleStage.caption: 49 mm titanium, or 46 and 42
appleStage.premise: Case and display to scale: the Ultra 4 at 49 by 44 millimetres.

scenes.narration: Both watches get an all-new Health Sensing System, and the payoff is one number. Apple's Vitals app reads your sleep, your recent activity and your heart rate variability, and turns all three into a daily readiness score: pace yourself, ready, or go for it. That only works because the sensor samples often enough to show a trend rather than a moment, and a trend is the only thing worth acting on when you have just woken up.

appleStage.headline: One number: [Readiness]
appleStage.caption: Vitals, on the watch face
appleStage.premise: Sleep, activity and heart rate variability, resolved into one word each morning.

scenes.narration: Battery is where the Ultra 4 stops being a bigger Series 12. Fifty hours of everyday use, eighty four hours in low power mode, and ten hours of outdoor workout tracking — a quarter more than the last Ultra managed. Ten hours is the figure that matters, because a long day out is exactly when you can't stop to charge.

appleStage.headline: Ultra 4: [50 hours] everyday
appleStage.caption: Battery, by mode
appleStage.premise: Apple's figures for the Ultra 4, in hours, by how the watch is being used.

scenes.narration: AirPods 5 closed the hardware out, and the interesting part isn't the sound. These buds cancel noise in an open-ear design, with no rubber tip sealing your ear canal — which means no physical blocking to help, so every decibel you don't hear was cancelled by the H2 chip using three microphones and an accelerometer that feels your jaw move.

appleStage.headline: Noise cancelled, [ear open]
appleStage.caption: AirPods 5, case and bud
appleStage.premise: Case and bud to the same scale, from Apple's published dimensions.

scenes.narration: Apple's claim for that is one and a half times more noise cancellation than AirPods 4, which it calls the best in an open-ear design. AirPods 5 start at a hundred and twenty nine dollars.

appleStage.headline: [1.5x] more than AirPods 4
appleStage.caption: Apple's own relative figure
appleStage.premise: AirPods 4 as the baseline, AirPods 5 against it, using Apple's own comparison.

scenes.narration: So what does all of it cost? An iPhone 18 Pro starts at eleven ninety nine for two hundred and fifty six gigabytes, and the rungs above it get steep quickly: two hundred dollars to five twelve, four hundred more for a terabyte, and six hundred on top of that for two. Storage is where Apple makes its margin, and this year the steps are wider.

appleStage.headline: Each step costs [more] than the last
appleStage.caption: iPhone 18 Pro, US pricing
appleStage.premise: The chip beside each row is the step up from the row above it.

scenes.narration: And here's where the event got strange. Normally last year's iPhones drop in price the morning a new one arrives. Instead, Apple raised every one of them by a hundred dollars on the same afternoon — the 16, the 17, the 17e and the Air. Each dim bar is what that phone cost the day before, and the lit part is what got added.

appleStage.headline: The old iPhones got [more expensive]
appleStage.caption: US prices, the same afternoon
appleStage.premise: Each bar runs to the old price; the glowing extension is what Apple added to it.

scenes.narration: Memory is the reason, and the scale is worth seeing. A two hundred and fifty six gigabyte memory chip costs four hundred percent more than a year ago, because the AI data centres are buying the same parts. What you pay went up nine percent, while the bill of materials rose about thirty eight — so Apple ate most of the difference, which it does not usually do.

appleStage.headline: You pay [9%] more. Memory costs 400% more.
appleStage.caption: Year-on-year change
appleStage.premise: Three different numbers, all percentages, all year on year — and only one is yours.

scenes.narration: That's the event: a camera that changes its own aperture, a phone that folds without a hole in the screen, a watch that answers one question a day, and buds that cancel noise with your ear open. Each product has its own video on the channel.
